title: Chemical properties of matter
competency: Identify chemical properties and distinguish them from physical properties.

keywords.def: Describes how a substance changes, or resists change, to form a new substance.
The ability of a substance to burn.
How a substance reacts with other substances.

en.text: A chemical property describes how a substance changes, or resists change, to form a new substance. We cannot find it just by looking or touching. Flammability and reactivity are chemical properties. Iron rusting in moist air shows a chemical property of iron.

screens.title: Will it burn?
screens.ask: Paper burns but a stone does not. Can you tell this just by looking at them?
opts: No, you must try to change them
screens.after: You cannot see flammability. You find it only when the substance changes (or does not). That is a chemical property.

screens.title: 2.2.2 Chemical properties of matter
paras: A chemical property describes how a substance undergoes or resists change to form a new substance.
It cannot be found just by viewing or touching the substance.
Flammability is one chemical property. Reactivity is another.

screens.title: Table 2.2 Physical and chemical properties
table: Describe how a substance changes to form a new one
Cannot be seen just by looking or touching
Internal structure must be affected to test it
Colour, density, volume, melting point, boiling point, conductivity

screens.title: Key words
defs: Describes how a substance changes, or resists change, to form a new substance.
The ability of a substance to burn.
How a substance reacts with other substances.

screens.why: Flammability describes forming new substances by burning.
screens.clue: Which one is about forming something new?

items: Mercury is liquid at room temperature
Nickel dissolves in acid to give a green solution
Silver shows no reaction in hydrochloric acid
screens.why: Chemical: how it reacts or resists reacting. Physical: observed without change.
screens.clue: Does a new substance form, or could it?

screens.text: A chemical property can be found just by looking at a substance.
screens.why: The substance must be changed (or tried) to see its chemical property.

screens.text: "Silver shows no sign of reaction in hydrochloric acid." Why is this a CHEMICAL property, even though nothing happens?
opts: It describes how silver resists change
screens.ans: It describes how silver resists change
screens.why: A chemical property describes how a substance undergoes OR resists change. Silver's low reactivity is a chemical property.
screens.clue: Read the definition carefully: "undergoes or resists".

items.title: 1. Physical or chemical? (a–e)
items: a. Iron rusts in moist air
b. Mercury is a liquid at room temperature
c. Nickel dissolves in acid to give a green solution
items.why: Rusting and reacting with acid form new substances.

items.title: 1. Physical or chemical? (f–j)
items: f. Titanium can be drawn into thin wires
g. Inhaled beryllium dust causes lung disease
h. Silver shows no reaction in hydrochloric acid
i. Lead is denser than aluminium
items.why: Chemical properties describe reacting or resisting reaction.

items.title: 2. Intensive or extensive?
items.why: Extensive properties depend on the amount; intensive ones do not.

items.title: 3. Sense organs or measurable?
items.why: Colour, odour and taste are sensed; the rest need apparatus.

test.why: Flammability describes burning to form new substances.

test.text: Reactivity between two substances is a chemical property.
test.why: The book names reactivity as a chemical property.

test.text: "Iron metal rusts in moist air" describes a …
Which statement is true of chemical properties?
opts: They are easily seen by looking
They describe how a substance forms new substances
They are the same as colour
test.ans: They describe how a substance forms new substances

items: Iron is attracted by a magnet
test.why: Burning and reacting are chemical; colour and magnetism are physical.
